neighbours.label: 'view' / 'panorama' as a visual depiction of a scene or object (an aerial view, a front view, a panorama of hills), as against 'view' meaning opinion
fire: The postcard shows an aerial view of the castle and its gardens.
In the diagram, a side view of the skull reveals the jaw joint.
From the summit there is a panorama of lakes and pine forests.
The drawing gives a top view of the house with every room labelled.
The photographer took a wide view of the harbour at sunrise.
Plate 12 offers a rear view of the cathedral and its towers.
The balcony offers a sweeping panorama of the old city.
Figure 5 shows a cross-section view of the turbine blade.
quiet: The councillor said that, in her view, the castle needed new gardens.
In the textbook, the chapter on the skull explains the jaw joint.
From the summit we walked down to the lakes and pine forests.
The architect's opinion was that the house needed more rooms.
The photographer arrived at the harbour just before sunrise.
Plate 12 lists the cost of repairing the cathedral towers.
The balcony was repaired after the storm last winter.
In his view, the turbine blade was too heavy for the design.
